description: Grand Isle: Louisiana's First Line of Defense from Coastal Flooding is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Jacques Cousteau National Estuarine Research Reserve; Rutgers University | Center for Remote Sensing and Spatial Analysis; USACE, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Lying directly south of New Orleans on Louisiana’s coast, Grand Isle often bears the brunt of strong waves and storm surge in the Gulf of America (formerly known as the Gulf of Mexico). To protect this town and inland parishes from flooding, engineers constructed a first line of defense. Coverage: Louisiana (2014). The toolkit gives Louisiana as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: At Grand Isle, Louisiana, rising seas and sinking land add up to one of the highest rates of relative sea level rise in the world. As global sea level goes up and regional geologic processes cause the ground to go down, Gulf waters claim hundreds of acres of land per year.
